correctness.rationale: For p≥13 the sextic-in-x substitution gives a squarefree degree-twelve polynomial exactly off A=±2, so the smooth projective model has genus five. In the basis x^(j−1)dx/y the unrooted coefficient at row i, column j is [x^(pi−j)](x^12+A x^6+1)^((p−1)/2). Its support is j=i for p≡1 mod 6 and j=6−i for p≡−1 mod 6. Dividing the first three exponents by six and reflecting the other two by reciprocity gives degrees (r,2r,3r) and (r−1,2r−1,3r−1), respectively. Truncating the binomial series to degree m=(p−1)/2 is valid modulo p, giving the coefficient (−1)^d P_d(A/2). Inverse Frobenius is an automorphism of the algebraically closed ground field; on each matched one- or two-dimensional orbit Cartier is bijective when its coefficient is nonzero and zero otherwise, so 2,2,1 are stable-rank weights. The reversal in dimension five is even, leaving the determinant sign (−1)^d3. The Legendre leading coefficient 4^(−d)·binom(2d,d) is nonzero, and L_d(±2)=(±1)^d. The differential equation with leading factor A²−4 rules out a double root by successive differentiation because d<p. Hence all divisor and determinant degrees and the additivity of multiplicities at intersections follow on the smooth parameter line. Independent replay in branches/cartier_check.py used Rodrigues' formula and repeated bivariate multiplication for p=13,17,19,23, checking every symbolic entry and squarefreeness. The monic pairwise gcds in order (1,2),(1,3),(2,3) were (1,1,1) at 13 and (1,A,1) at 19. Thus the stated rank counts are correct: six of rank three and six of rank four at 13; one of rank two and eight each of ranks three and four at 19. The bounded checks corroborate the proof, not replace it; the frozen checker was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Novoselov's theorem is for general g over finite fields, and its proof is an identity of coefficient polynomials in ρ. Equality on all finite extensions also implies the polynomial identity, so it applies to A in every algebraically closed field of the given characteristic.

Ohashi–Kudo give Jac(H) isogenous to E1×E2×E3×E4² via genus-two and genus-three quotients, and their Proposition 4.11 tests the simultaneous vanishing of three truncated series in a transformed parameter δ.
The cited generalized Legendre manuscript was identified bibliographically, but its text was not obtained.

Ohashi–Kudo's isogeny also reduces p-rank to elliptic ordinarity, but their simultaneous-vanishing criterion considered alone does not enumerate intermediate ranks or give the determinant in the original basis.

evidence: Upon specialization the prior matrix has orbits {1,5},{2,4},{3} with equal entries within each pair (separate equal diagonal entries when p≡1 mod 6). Nonzero scalar orbits are invariant and bijective after Frobenius twisting; zeros remove the whole corresponding weight. The reversal has sign +1.

The already determined P_d factors have d≤(p−1)/2, so 4^(−d)·binom(2d,d) is nonzero and ±2 are not roots. A double root elsewhere contradicts the Legendre differential equation and d<p. The determinant therefore has precisely the stated weighted reduced divisors with additive overlaps.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior theorem fixes the entire normalized matrix; all-prime rank, determinant and reduced degrees are direct consequences with classical polynomial properties. No new criterion for intersections at general p is established; the remaining finite examples use low-degree Euclidean algorithms on the same polynomials.

originality.rationale: Novoselov (2017), §2.2 Theorem 9(1)–(6) and proof, already gives the same coefficient matrix for the general even-degree family y²=x^(2g+2)−2ρx^(g+1)+1. Setting g=5 and ρ=−A/2 gives precisely the three Legendre entries with the same diagonal or antidiagonal arrangement and repetition. The exact determinant and geometric p-rank follow by multiplication and immediate counting of the nonzero Frobenius-permuted blocks. The reduced factors, degrees and multiplicities then follow from classical Legendre identities; allowing transcendental A changes nothing because the matrix formula is polynomial. The two small-prime gcds are correct worked instances, not a distinct uniform intersection result. This is demonstrated prior coverage of the principal finding, not a verdict based on unavailable sources.
residual_risks: The full generalized Legendre manuscript and same-family characteristic-seven record were not obtained, so they could provide additional coverage. They are immaterial to the demonstrated implication from Novoselov.
No priority conclusion is made about the two finite gcd evaluations in isolation.

value.rationale: The family and its geometric p-rank are mathematically natural, but the central result is an index specialization of a known explicit matrix followed by direct orbit counting and standard Legendre facts. Its two low-degree gcd examples illustrate how an overlap changes rank but do not establish a new intersection criterion, boundary or independently motivated exact gap. The correct specialization and examples are useful exposition, not a separate research finding here.
